text: In sixteen forty-five, if your baby fell sick, you didn't fetch a doctor.
You boiled a bottle of pins.
That winter, I was nine. Six of us in one room. The pig behind a hurdle. Smoke in the rafters.
Three babies in our lane had died since harvest.
Then my sister started to cough.
Gran said it wasn't the cold. It was someone.
She took down the stone jug with the bearded face.
Bent pins. Iron nails. A lock of the baby's hair.
And one long grey hair, from a comb I'd never seen.
She set it in the embers, and told me the rule.
Whoever cursed the baby would feel every pin. In her own body.
And she'd have to come to our door to make it stop.
We sat up. The fire ticked. The jug began to hiss.
At midnight, the baby stopped coughing.
Gran didn't move. She said, open it.
